newsitem.title: UK: UK supermarket shares drop on sector switching.
newsitem.headline: UK supermarket shares drop on sector switching.

text.p: British supermarket shares dropped on Tuesday as investors took profits and switched into sectors benefiting from a sudden drop in the strength of sterling, dealers said.
The supermarkets sector has been boosted in recent months by strong domestic demand and insulation from the effects of a strengthening pound.
The currency's decline against the mark this week has encouraged investors to switch out of supermarkets into sterling-sensitive sectors like engineering, dealers said.
"Everybody piled into the domestic-earners when sterling was going up, and now it's come off a bit they are getting bashed," one market-maker said. "It might be a time to take profits."
Tesco Plc was 12p weaker at 416-1/2 by 0906 GMT. Safeway Plc dropped 11p to 386, J. Sainsbury Plc fell six pence to 430-1/2 and ASDA Group Plc lost 3-3/4p to 144.
